# Pork and cabbage stir-fry with rice

Stir-fry sauces from a jar are often very high in sodium. This sauce uses 1 tablespoon of reduced-sodium soy sauce for 4 people, with ginger, garlic, honey and vinegar. Cabbage and red pepper stay crisp and are lower-potassium choices than broccoli or spinach.

**Serves 4** · 30 minutes · Lower potassium · Lower phosphorus · Dialysis-friendly

!!! abstract "Carbohydrate per serving"
    **47 g carbohydrate** (about 3 carb choices of 15 g). It comes from the rice, the honey and the vegetables. For about 55 g, add ¼ cup more rice (11 g).

## Ingredients

| Ingredient | Amount | Grams |
|---|---|---|
| Pork tenderloin, roasted | 10 oz pork tenderloin, cooked weight (about 14 oz raw), cut in thin strips | 284 g |
| Canola oil | 2 tbsp canola oil | 28 g |
| Cabbage, raw | 2 cups sliced green cabbage | 140 g |
| Bell pepper, red, raw | 1 cup red bell pepper strips | 150 g |
| Onion, raw | ½ cup sliced onion | 80 g |
| Garlic, raw | 2 cloves garlic, chopped | 6.0 g |
| Ginger root, fresh | 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger | 6.0 g |
| Soy sauce, reduced sodium | 1 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce | 14 g |
| Honey | 1 tbsp honey | 21 g |
| Vinegar, cider | 1 tbsp cider or rice vinegar | 15 g |
| Cornstarch | 1 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with 3 tbsp water | 8.0 g |
| Rice, white, long-grain, cooked | 3 cups cooked white rice, cooked without salt | 474 g |

## Steps

1. Mix the soy sauce, honey, vinegar and cornstarch with 3 tablespoons of water.
2. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Stir-fry the raw pork strips for 3–4 minutes until no longer pink (145 °F, 63 °C), then lift them out.
3. Add the rest of the oil, then the onion, cabbage and pepper. Stir-fry for 3 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute more.
4. Return the pork, pour in the sauce and stir until it thickens and coats everything, about 1 minute. Serve over ¾ cup rice.

## Why it works for kidneys

- Pork tenderloin has more potassium than chicken (about 360 mg per 3 oz), so this recipe uses 2½ oz a serving and lower-potassium vegetables to stay under 600 mg.
- Pick plain pork, not "enhanced" or marinated pork, which has added sodium and phosphate.
- The cornstarch thickens the sauce, so you need less soy sauce for the same flavour.

## Make it fit you

- **Chicken instead of pork:** the same weight of chicken breast or thigh; it lowers potassium a little.
- **More vegetables:** bean sprouts, snow peas or water chestnuts are lower-potassium stir-fry choices.
- **On dialysis:** use 12 oz cooked pork for 4 (3 oz each) if your team wants more protein; potassium rises to about 600 mg a serving, the top of the line.
